region.text: Eastern Arabia including the islands of Bahrain, with al-Ahsa

ledger.note: 1253: the Usfurids take Eastern Arabia. The dynasty 'in 1253 gained control of Eastern Arabia, including the islands of Bahrain'; infobox 'Established: 1253', 'Capital: al-Ahsa'; they overthrew the Uyunids (the page gives no separate year).

1392: the Jarwanids supplant the Usfurids. Usfurids infobox 'Disestablished: 1392'; 'After 150 years of rule the Usfurids were overthrown by the Jarwanids'. The Jarwanid page instead says their dynasty was 'Established: 1310' and came to power 'some time in the 14th century, after expelling the forces of Sa'eed ibn Mughamis', so the two lines overlapped (Qatif and al-Ahsa) and the year is the Usfurid page's.
1392: the seat moves from al-Ahsa to Qatif. Jarwanid infobox 'Capital: Qatif'.

1417: the Jabrids replace the Jarwanids. Jabrids infobox 'Established: 1417'; the elder brother of Ajwad ibn Zamil took the throne 'deposing and killing the last Jarwanid ruler in Qatif' in the 'early 15th century'; the Jarwanid infobox ends in 1417.

1521: the Portuguese take Bahrain. 'In 1521, the Portuguese Empire conquered the Awal Islands' from Muqrin ibn Zamil, the Jabrid ruler, who 'fell in battle in Bahrain' (Jabrids page); the Hormuz page: 'the 1521 invasion of Bahrain that ended Jabrid rule of the Persian Gulf archipelago'.

region.text: Al-Ahsa and Qatif, the mainland remnant

ledger.note: 1521: Jabrid rule ends on the Bahrain islands and the state is closed. The mainland remained partly Jabrid ('Jabrid rule remained in effect in some regions', infobox end 1524, last ruler Ghossib bin Hilal) until 'In 1550, Al-Ahsa and nearby Qatif came under the sovereignty of the Ottoman Empire' (Al-Ahsa page).

wars.name: Jabrid-Hormuz tribute dispute
wars.outcome: The Jabrids retook the Bahrain islands from the princes of Hormuz (undated, Al-Ahsa page); the Jabrid king Muqrin ibn Zamil 'had refused to pay the tribute Hormuz demanded' (Hormuz page); the Jabrid ruler 'was nominally a vassal of Hormuz'.
wars.note: The pages date neither the retaking nor the dispute; the span is the whole Jabrid period (1417-1521).

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of Bahrain
wars.outcome: The Portuguese conquered the Awal Islands in 1521 from Muqrin ibn Zamil, ending Jabrid rule of the archipelago.

certainty.note: No survey lines: the Gulf-coast shape (Kuwait to the northern UAE, Qatar) and the desert frontier towards Najd are approximate, and the pages opened give no extent beyond 'Eastern Arabia'.

notes:
Cliopatria row: 'Bahrani Dynasty' 1260-1520 (Wikipedia title 'Al-Ahsa Oasis') is a chain of three dynasties of Eastern Arabia, Usfurids (1253-1392), Jarwanids (1310-1417, Qatif) and Jabrids (1417-1524); treated as one state with two renames (1392, 1417). The pages disagree on the overlap: the Jarwanid page says established 1310, the Usfurid page ends in 1392 'overthrown by the Jarwanids'. The Hormuz article says the Jabrid king was 'nominally a vassal of Hormuz' and that Hormuz's realm 'extended as far as Bahrain in the west at its zenith' (citation needed); none of the five pages dates Hormuz's rule of Bahrain, Jabrid tribute, or the retaking of the islands.
Cliopatria shape: 70-74,000 km2 along the Gulf coast (Kuwait to the northern UAE, all of Qatar, Qatif, Bahrain), but not the capital oasis of al-Ahsa/Hofuf (0 of 12 cells); every keyframe is adjusted by adding Hofuf. The Qatar and northern-UAE parts of the shape are not supported by any page opened. The five small shape changes (1440, 1468, 1475) are not explained (unverified: page budget).
End year: Cliopatria 1520, Jabrids infobox 1524, Portuguese Bahrain 1521, Ottoman al-Hasa 1550; the dossier closes in 1521. The Cliopatria neighbours Mahdids (Oman) and the Mongols/Ilkhanate/Jalayirids/Timurids are not shown by any page as touching this state; the Safavids appear only from 1507.
Counterparts that need dossiers: kingdom-of-hormuz (c. 1300-1622; the Cliopatria set lacks a Hormuz row). The Muntafiq and Bani Khalid are successors only on the Jabrids infobox.
